purpose: Design of the /forge:start-requirements dispatcher skill and its three mode workflows (interactive, reverse-engineering, from-figma) for creating requirements documents.
summary: Overview of the dispatcher design: SKILL.md selects mode and delegates to self-contained workflow files
File layout of the start-requirements skill and its three workflow docs
Flowchart of mode selection and per-mode phases through review, ToC update and commit
Dispatcher responsibilities and the common rule for decisions made just before writing the requirements file
Decision order: completely-new check, additive vs differential type approval, feature, output directory, file name
Interactive mode: draft-driven, no up-front context collection, type judgment, temporary marker, glossary
Reverse-engineering mode: bulk context collection and source code analysis phases
From-figma mode: Figma MCP prerequisite, design tokens, SCR/CMP/FNC and static assets
Design principles: focus on What, per-mode context collection, workflow self-containment, ID consistency
Related files table for the skill, workflows and format docs
tasks: Modifying the start-requirements skill or its workflow files
Creating requirements documents in interactive mode
Deriving requirements from existing source code
Deciding feature, output location and file name for a new requirements document
Judging additive versus differential development type
